questions.q: What are the four steps of the minimal RAG pipeline built in this lesson?
options: Train, validate, test, deploy
Index, retrieve, assemble the prompt, generate
Tokenize, embed, decode, sample
Clean, split, fit, score
questions.explain: Documents are indexed once; each question retrieves the closest documents, which are assembled into a prompt that the model then answers from.

questions.q: The question "What is the airspeed of a swallow?" returned no documents. Why is that the desired behavior?
options: The vectorizer crashed on the question
Every score fell below min_score, so the pipeline can say it doesn't know instead of answering from irrelevant text
TF-IDF cannot process questions about animals
The threshold removes all documents whenever k is 2
questions.explain: A minimum similarity score stops unrelated questions from pulling in weak matches that the model might then use to invent an answer.

questions.q: "How long do I have to send an item back?" retrieved nothing even though the returns policy answers it. What is the cause?
options: TF-IDF matches shared words, and the question shares none with the returns document
The returns document was not indexed
Cosine similarity cannot be computed for short questions
The stop_words setting removed every word
questions.explain: Lexical retrieval compares words, not meaning. Embeddings compare meaning, which is why they handle paraphrases like send back versus return.

questions.q: Why does the prompt say to answer using ONLY the context and to say "I don't know" otherwise?
options: It makes the API call cheaper by removing the question
It keeps the answer grounded in the retrieved text and reduces made-up answers
It forces the model to output JSON
It lets the model see documents that were not retrieved
questions.explain: Grounding instructions tell the model to rely on the supplied context, which is the point of retrieval-augmented generation.

questions.q: Why is call_llm kept as a narrow function that takes text and returns text?
options: Because hosted APIs only accept a single string
So you can swap providers, or replace it with a fake in tests, without changing the retrieval code
Because it must run locally without a network
Because retrieval and generation cannot share variables
questions.explain: A small interface isolates the provider-specific part of the pipeline, making the rest testable and easy to change.
